## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Verses from the text share extensive passage-level parallels across early Buddhist literature [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Canon, parallels occur in other *Theragāthā* poems (Thag 2.2, Thag 4.3, and Thag 18.1), the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 6), the *Kosambiyajātaka* (Ja 428), the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128), and the Vinaya *Kosambakakkhandhaka* (Kd 10) [SuttaCentral]. Outside Pali, passage-level parallels are found in the Gilgit *Mūlasarvāstivādivinaya* (III.ii.183), the Patna Dharmapada (*Khāntivagga*, P-Dhp 239–260), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 14 *Drohavarga*) and its Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 14), as well as early Chinese translations of verse collections (T 210.9 and T 213.14) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral additionally records resembling parallels in Jain Prakrit literature, specifically *Sūyagaḍaṅgasutta* 1 and *Isibhāsiyāiṁ* 4 [SuttaCentral].
According to DharmaNexus, the poem shares twenty passages with three Pali works, most notably with the commentary *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (sixteen matching units, with the longest span covering segments §3.1–8.7), as well as two didactic Pali nīti anthologies: the *Mahārahanīti* (§6.4–8.6) and the *Dhammanīti* (§7.2–8.6) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records a low-plausibility cross-language alignment between segment §1.2 and the Tibetan translation of the *Ārya-maitreyamahāsiṃhanādanāmamahāyānasūtra* (D0067) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
